steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the http module from Node.js to enable creating HTTP servers and handling requests.
steps.hint: Use the built-in require() function to import Node.js modules. The http module is part of Node.js core.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing a core Node.js module
const fs = require('fs');
steps.expectedOutcome: The http module is imported and available for use in your code.
successCriteria: The http module is imported using require('http').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the http module, which provides the foundation for building HTTP servers in Node.js.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing the correct module. Use require('http') to import the HTTP module.
steps.feedbackWrong: The http module wasn't imported correctly. Remember to use require('http') to import the HTTP functionality.

steps.title: Create a basic HTTP server
steps.instruction: Create an HTTP server using the imported http module's createServer() method and make it listen on port 3000.
steps.hint: Use http.createServer() to create a server instance, then call .listen(3000) on it. You can pass an empty request handler function for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: A basic HTTP server that listens on port 3000 will be created.
successCriteria: An HTTP server is created using http.createServer() and configured to listen on port 3000.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a basic HTTP server that listens on port 3000.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using http.createServer() and calling .listen(3000) on the server instance.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server wasn't created correctly. Remember to use http.createServer() and make it listen on port 3000.

steps.title: Define the response envelope structure
steps.instruction: Create a function named createResponseEnvelope that returns an object with success, data, message, and timestamp properties. The function should take data, success (default true), and message (default empty string) as parameters.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns an object with the required properties. Use Date.now() for the timestamp.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a reusable function that standardizes API responses with consistent structure.
successCriteria: The createResponseEnvelope function exists and returns an object containing success, data, message, and timestamp properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a standardized response envelope function that will make your API responses consistent and predictable.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function returns an object with all four required properties: success, data, message, and timestamp.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function should return an object with success, data, message, and timestamp properties. Check that you're using the correct parameter names and including all required fields.

steps.title: Create a success response helper
steps.instruction: Create a function named createSuccessResponse that takes data and an optional message parameter, then returns a formatted success envelope object.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns an object with success: true, data, and message properties. The message should default to 'Operation successful' if not provided.
steps.expectedOutcome: A createSuccessResponse function that returns a properly structured success envelope object.
successCriteria: The createSuccessResponse function exists, takes data and optional message parameters, and returns an object with success: true, data, and message properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the success response helper function with the correct structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function returns an object with success: true, data, and message properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Check that it takes data and optional message parameters and returns the correct envelope structure.

steps.title: Create an error response helper
steps.instruction: Create a function named createErrorResponse that takes an error message and an optional status code, then returns a formatted error envelope object.
steps.hint: The function should return an object with success: false, message, and status properties. Use the status parameter or default to 500.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a createErrorResponse function that returns a structured error envelope object.
successCriteria: The createErrorResponse function exists, accepts message and optional status parameters, and returns an object with success: false, message, and status properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the error response helper function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function returns an object with success: false, message, and status properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Check that it accepts parameters and returns the correct error envelope structure.

steps.title: Set up route handling for the server
steps.instruction: Inside the server callback function, add conditional logic to check the request URL and handle different routes.
steps.hint: Use an if-else statement to check req.url and respond with different messages for '/' and '/api' routes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will respond with different plain text messages based on the requested URL path.
successCriteria: The server callback contains conditional logic that checks req.url and responds appropriately for at least two routes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented basic route handling in your HTTP server.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some route handling, but make sure to check req.url and handle at least two different routes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route handling logic is missing or incorrect. Check if you're properly checking req.url and responding with different messages.

steps.title: Implement a success route
steps.instruction: Inside the server's request handler, add a conditional check for the '/success' route. If the request URL matches, call the createSuccessResponse helper with a sample message and send the response using res.end().
steps.hint: Check req.url to match the route, then use your success helper to generate a standardized response envelope.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will now respond to GET requests to '/success' with a standardized success envelope containing a sample message.
successCriteria: The server's request handler includes a conditional check for '/success' that uses createSuccessResponse and sends the response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the success route using your helper function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the route check, but make sure to call createSuccessResponse and send the response properly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The success route isn't implemented correctly. Check if you're matching the URL and using the helper function.

steps.title: Implement an error route
steps.instruction: Inside the server's request handler, add an else-if condition to handle requests to the '/error' path. Use the createErrorResponse helper to generate an error response envelope and send it with a 500 status code.
steps.hint: Check if req.url equals '/error', then call createErrorResponse with an error message and code, and use res.writeHead and res.end to send the response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will now respond to requests to '/error' with a structured error response envelope containing the provided error message and code.
successCriteria: An else-if condition for '/error' is added, createErrorResponse is called with a message and code, and the response is sent with a 500 status and JSON content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the error route, allowing the server to return structured error responses.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're checking for '/error', calling createErrorResponse, and sending the response with status 500 and JSON content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error route isn't implemented correctly. Review the route handling pattern used for '/success' and adapt it for errors.

steps.title: Add proper response headers
steps.instruction: Add Content-Type and Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers to the success route response.
steps.hint: Use res.writeHead() to set both headers before sending the response. The Content-Type should be 'application/json' and Access-Control-Allow-Origin can be '*' for development.
steps.expectedOutcome: The success route will now include proper headers for JSON responses and CORS.
successCriteria: The success route handler includes res.writeHead() with both Content-Type and Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the proper headers to ensure your API responses are correctly formatted and accessible from different origins.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include both Content-Type and Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers in the res.writeHead() call.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the hint: you need to add headers using res.writeHead() before sending the response in the success route.

steps.title: Handle 404 routes
steps.instruction: Add a default route handler in the server callback that returns a 404 error response using your createErrorResponse helper for any unknown routes.
steps.hint: After your existing route checks, add an else/default case that uses createErrorResponse with a 'Not Found' message and error code 404, then sends it as the response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will now respond with a standardized error envelope for any route that isn't '/success', returning a 404 status message.
successCriteria: A default route handler is added that uses createErrorResponse with 'Not Found' (or similar) message and error code 404, and sends the response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your server now handles unknown routes with a proper standardized error response.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a default handler, but check that it uses createErrorResponse with appropriate message and error code 404.
steps.feedbackWrong: The default route handler is missing or doesn't use the error response helper correctly.
